NAME: Paginated Invoice Loader
DESC:
A billing API exposes invoices through page-number pagination. You must load all invoices into a summary while protecting the pipeline against a misbehaving API. You do not make real HTTP calls: the API is given to you as a function.

API

fetch_page(page, page_size) returns a dict such as:

{
    "page": 2,
    "page_size": 3,
    "total_count": 7,
    "results": [
        {"invoice_id": "INV-4", "amount": 10.25, "currency": " eur ", "status": "paid"},
        ...
    ]
}
  • Pages are numbered from 1. A page contains at most page_size records. A page after the last one returns an empty results list.
  • total_count is computed by the server at request time and is not reliable: invoices can be created while you paginate, which also means that the same invoice can appear on two consecutive pages.
  • fetch_page can raise an exception (timeout, server error).
  • In a record, amount is a number or a numeric string, possibly with more than 2 decimals (120.5, "99.999", " 5.05 "); currency is a 3-letter code with arbitrary case and spaces; status is a free-text string such as "paid", "Paid" or " VOID ".

Rules

  1. Request pages 1, 2, 3, ... in order, passing page_size unchanged.
  2. Stop after the first page whose results contains fewer than page_size records (an empty page included). Never request a page after that.
  3. Never request more than max_pages pages in total.
  4. If fetch_page raises an exception, stop immediately: keep everything loaded from the previous pages and do not request any other page.
  5. An invoice whose invoice_id was already seen on a previous page is a duplicate: skip it and count it in duplicates_skipped.
  6. An invoice whose status, ignoring case and surrounding spaces, is void is not counted in invoice_count nor in totals (it still counts as seen for rule 5).
  7. totals maps each currency (trimmed, uppercase) to the sum of the amounts of its counted invoices, rounded to 2 decimals. Currencies without any counted invoice do not appear.
  8. complete is True if the loading stopped because of rule 2, and False otherwise (exception, or max_pages pages fetched with the last one full).

The sequence of pages you request is part of the grading.

Output

A dict with exactly these keys:

key type description
pages_fetched int number of calls to fetch_page that returned a response
complete bool see rule 8
invoice_count int number of distinct, non-void invoices
duplicates_skipped int see rule 5
totals dict[str, float] see rule 7

Example

page_size = 3, max_pages = 10

page results
1 INV-1 100.0 "MAD" paid ; INV-2 "50.5" "mad" paid ; INV-3 20 "EUR" void
2 INV-3 20 "EUR" void ; INV-4 10.25 " eur " paid ; INV-5 "30" "MAD" "Paid"
3 INV-6 5 "EUR" paid

Pages requested: 1, 2, 3 (page 3 has fewer than 3 records, so it is the last one).

Expected output

{
    "pages_fetched": 3,
    "complete": True,
    "invoice_count": 5,
    "duplicates_skipped": 1,
    "totals": {"MAD": 180.5, "EUR": 15.25},
}

Function signature

def load_invoices(fetch_page, page_size: int, max_pages: int) -> dict:
    ...

Constraints

  • Standard library only (json, math, datetime, ... are available).
  • 1 <= page_size <= 1000, 1 <= max_pages <= 1000.

The functions described in the task (the API) are provided by the tests: you only write your function.
SOLUTION:
def load_invoices(fetch_page, page_size: int, max_pages: int) -> dict:
    seen = set()
    totals = {}
    invoice_count = 0
    duplicates_skipped = 0
    pages_fetched = 0
    complete = False

    page = 1
    while page <= max_pages:                      # plafond dur : jamais plus de max_pages appels
        try:
            response = fetch_page(page, page_size)
        except Exception:                         # API en erreur : on garde ce qui est déjà chargé
            complete = False
            break
        pages_fetched += 1
        results = response.get("results") or []

        for record in results:
            invoice_id = record["invoice_id"]
            if invoice_id in seen:                # recouvrement entre pages (offset qui glisse)
                duplicates_skipped += 1
                continue
            seen.add(invoice_id)
            if str(record.get("status") or "").strip().lower() == "void":
                continue
            currency = str(record["currency"]).strip().upper()
            totals[currency] = totals.get(currency, 0.0) + float(record["amount"])
            invoice_count += 1

        if len(results) < page_size:              # page vide ou partielle = dernière page
            complete = True
            break
        page += 1
    # sortie de boucle par le plafond : complete reste False (la dernière page était pleine)

    return {
        "pages_fetched": pages_fetched,
        "complete": complete,
        "invoice_count": invoice_count,
        "duplicates_skipped": duplicates_skipped,
        "totals": {cur: round(amount, 2) for cur, amount in totals.items()},
    }
